name: touch
description: Change file access and modification time
porting_notes: Port of OpenBSD touch 1.27. Uses amiport_stat() for the stat-first pattern (check file exists before creating). utimes() shimmed via amiport_utimes() which sets AmigaOS modification time. strptime() available via libnix. Access time (-a flag) accepted but no-ops since OFS/FFS only store modification time. 20/21 FS-UAE tests pass; 1 failure is the -d %F format specifier which strptime does not support in libnix.
known_limitations: Access time not supported: AmigaOS filesystems (OFS/FFS) only store modification time; -a flag accepted but has no effect. The %F strptime format specifier is not recognized; use -d with explicit ISO 8601 format. File permissions (DEFFILEMODE) ignored since AmigaOS does not enforce Unix permission bits.

Short:        Change file access and modification time
Type:         util/cli
Architecture: m68k-amigaos >= 3.0
Uploader:     duncan (at) bowring (dot) us
Author:       The Regents of the University of California (ported by Duncan Bowring)
Version:      1.27

touch - Change file access and modification time

Original author: The Regents of the University of California
Ported by Duncan Bowring using amiport (AI-assisted porting toolkit).
Project: https://github.com/bdgscotland/amiport

Cross-compiled with m68k-amigaos-gcc for AmigaOS 3.x (68000+).
Tested in vamos emulator and FS-UAE.

Usage:
  touch [-acm] [-d ccyy-mm-ddTHH:MM:SS[.frac][Z]] [-r file]
        [-t [[cc]yy]mmddHHMM[.SS]] file ...

Options:
  -a      Change access time only (no effect on AmigaOS)
  -c      Do not create the file if it does not exist
  -d      Set time using ISO 8601 format
  -f      Ignored (compatibility)
  -m      Change modification time only
  -r file Use the timestamp of the reference file
  -t time Set time using [[CC]YY]MMDDhhmm[.SS] format

Note: AmigaOS stores only modification time. The -a flag is
accepted but has no effect since there is no access time field.

Includes full source code (original POSIX and ported Amiga versions)
and PORT.md documenting every transformation applied.
